chief_complaint: morning stiffness and pain in my hands
hpi_details: 35F presents with a 4-month history of pain, swelling, and stiffness in the small joints of both hands (MCPs and PIPs). The stiffness is worst in the morning and lasts for 2 hours.
concerns: worried her hands will become deformed

core_concepts: Symmetric polyarthritis involving small joints (MCP, PIP, sparing DIP).
common_misconceptions: Assuming osteoarthritis (which affects DIPs and has brief morning stiffness).
dangerous_errors: Delaying DMARD therapy, leading to irreversible joint destruction.
management_principles: Prompt rheumatology referral for clinician-directed DMARD therapy; methotrexate or a steroid bridge require pregnancy, infection, liver/kidney function, interaction, and monitoring review. NSAIDs require gastrointestinal, renal, cardiovascular, and anticoagulant-risk assessment.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Clinical Guidance

reference_soap.subjective: 35F with symmetric pain and swelling in hand joints and 2-hour morning stiffness.
reference_soap.objective: Bilateral MCP and PIP synovitis (swelling, warmth, tenderness). DIPs spared.
reference_soap.plan: Order RF, anti-CCP, ESR/CRP, CBC, renal/liver function, and hand radiographs; refer promptly to rheumatology for individualized DMARD planning. Screen pregnancy plans, infection risk, comorbidities, and medication interactions before immunosuppression; urgently assess an acutely hot joint with fever for septic arthritis.

learning_objectives: Differentiate RA from osteoarthritis based on joint pattern and morning stiffness.

teaching.one_liner: Symmetric polyarthritis of the small hand joints with prolonged morning stiffness in a young female.
red_flags: An acutely hot, severely painful joint with fever or systemic illness may be septic arthritis and needs urgent assessment.
New neurologic symptoms or neck pain after trauma in established RA warrants urgent assessment for cervical spine involvement.

must_ask.say: Are both hands affected in the same joints on each side?
How long does the stiffness in your hands last after you wake up?
How many months has this been going on, and is it getting worse?
Have you felt unusually tired, or had any low-grade fevers?
Is the stiffness making it hard to grip things or get dressed?

history.answer: My hands have been really stiff and painful every morning, and it is making it difficult to do my daily routines.
It hurts in both of my hands equally, especially the knuckles and the middle joints of my fingers.
history.topic: Location and symmetry of joint pain

history.answer: It started gradually about four months ago and has been steadily worsening.
It is a continuous, dull aching pain in the finger joints, usually about a 4 or 5 out of 10.
My knuckles and middle finger joints look puffy and feel warm to touch, but the skin is not red.
The stiffness is worst right when I wake up and takes about two hours of moving around to loosen up.
Moving my hands gently eases the stiffness over time, but heavy use makes the aching worse. Warm water showers give temporary relief.
In the mornings I struggle to open jars, turn door knobs, or button my work shirts because my grip feels so weak and stiff.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, I never injured my hands, and I haven't heard any popping sounds or felt joints catching.
No, I have never experienced joint pain or swelling like this before in my life.
I have been feeling unusually tired and drained over the past few months, but my weight has been stable.
No, I do not have any skin rashes, scaly patches, mouth sores, hair loss, red eyes, or dry mouth.
No, I do not have any morning back stiffness, heel tenderness, or swelling of my whole toes or fingers.
No, I have not had any diarrhea, painful urination, vaginal discharge, or sore throats recently.
No, I do not eat a lot of red meat or seafood, and I do not take water pills.
No, I have never had joint injections, joint surgeries, or taken steroid medications.
I have been in a faithful monogamous marriage with my husband for eight years and have no other partners.
I think I might be developing arthritis, maybe rheumatoid arthritis like my grandmother had.
I am really frightened that my finger joints will become permanently deformed and prevent me from working.
I hope to find out what is causing this swelling and start an effective treatment to stop it from getting worse.
I have no history of chronic medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or heart problems.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I take over-the-counter ibuprofen 400 milligrams as needed, which takes the edge off the pain for a few hours.
No, I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials.
I have smoked about half a pack of cigarettes a day for roughly 20 years, so about 10 pack-years.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine socially, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as an office administrator doing a lot of computer typing, and I live at home with my husband.
My maternal grandmother had rheumatoid arthritis, but my parents and brother do not have any joint conditions.
My last menstrual period started two weeks ago, and my monthly cycles are regular every 28 days.
We currently use condoms for birth control and I am not pregnant, though we are hoping to have another child in the next year or two.

exam.finding: A well-nourished woman appearing comfortable at rest, in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor or injection, and sclerae are anicteric.

Symmetric soft-tissue swelling, warmth, and tenderness across bilateral second and third MCP and PIP joints with painful limitation of full fist closure; DIP joints are spared without bony enlargements or deformities.
Full cervical and thoracolumbar spine range of motion without midline tenderness or pain on movement.
No subcutaneous nodules, psoriatic plaques, malar erythema, nail pitting, or tophi identified.
Gait is smooth, steady, and symmetric without antalgia.
